patterns_found.visual_evidence: The mobile sketch shows a compact header area with branding at top and no visible full navigation list, while the desktop sketch shows multiple top-right nav items/icons. This cross-viewport difference strongly implies the desktop nav collapses into a mobile menu trigger.
patterns_found.behavior_notes: A menu button should toggle the primary navigation open/closed on mobile. It should expose the same destinations visible in desktop navigation and indicate expanded/collapsed state.
patterns_found.ambiguities: The exact trigger icon and whether the menu opens as a dropdown, drawer, or full-screen panel are not clear from the sketch.

patterns_found.visual_evidence: Both sketches depict a large primary image with a row/grid of smaller thumbnail images beneath or nearby, a common gallery pattern implying enlarged image viewing when a thumbnail or hero image is activated.
patterns_found.behavior_notes: Activating a thumbnail should likely open a larger image view or replace the hero image; if implemented as a lightbox overlay, it needs open/close behavior, focus handling, and dismissal via close control/Escape/backdrop.
patterns_found.ambiguities: The sketch does not explicitly show an overlay state, so this could alternatively be an inline image swap rather than a modal lightbox.

patterns_found.visual_evidence: The lower content area in both sketches includes a comments/discussion-like section with bullet-style entries and supporting text blocks, consistent with a comment form or submission area shown in the reference structure.
patterns_found.behavior_notes: If a comment form is present as implied by the page type, required fields and submission errors should be validated client-side and surfaced clearly.
patterns_found.ambiguities: The sketches do not explicitly draw input fields, labels, or buttons, so the presence of a form is inferred from page context rather than clearly visible controls.

patterns_found.visual_evidence: The page is very long in both mobile and desktop sketches, with substantial content extending far below the fold. Long editorial/gallery pages commonly include a return-to-top control; the reference HTML also contains a back-to-top link.
patterns_found.behavior_notes: A back-to-top control should scroll the page to the top, ideally appearing after some scrolling or remaining available near the footer.
patterns_found.ambiguities: The sketch does not clearly depict the control itself, so the need is inferred from page length and page type.

sketch_notes: The sketches imply a mostly content-driven waterfall detail page with limited but important JavaScript: mobile navigation collapse, image-gallery interaction, likely comment-form validation, and long-page convenience behavior like back-to-top. The main cross-viewport difference is navigation treatment: desktop appears to expose top-level nav directly, while mobile likely requires a collapsed menu. Gallery behavior is suggested in both layouts by the prominent hero image plus thumbnails, but whether that interaction is an inline image swap or a true lightbox overlay remains the biggest uncertainty.
